slides.texte_overlay:
How to speak like a man
people take seriously
Stop asking for permission to speak. Skip "sorry, can I just say..." and say it. Confident openings make people listen from the first word.
Use fewer qualifiers. "Kind of," "maybe," "I guess." Each one makes your point weaker. Say what you mean plainly. Clear words make strong points.
Breathe from your belly. A voice supported by deep breathing sounds fuller and calmer than one squeezed from the throat. Your voice will sound deeper and more relaxed.
Make one point at a time. Finish one idea before starting the next. People follow you better and remember what you said. Pause between points.
Before: I spoke a lot but said little. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and now my ideas have more substance.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: I spoke a lot but said little. After: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Now my ideas have more substance.

slides.texte_overlay: Keep your hands calm. Slow, open gestures support your words. Fidgeting distracts people from what you're saying. Keep your hands relaxed at your sides when you're not using them.
Say "I don't know" when you don't. Honesty about the limits of your knowledge makes everything else you say more credible. People trust honest men.
